raw.details:
Break Vulnerabilities. Engineer Trust. Secure Communication

Protocol Zero is a multi-stage cybersecurity competition focused on the security of modern communication systems and Secure Communication Protocol. Participate in an online Mini-CTF, expert-led Bootcamp, six-week Hackathon and onsite Attack-Defence CTF. Learn applied cryptography, build secure communication systems, identify vulnerabilities and compete for cash prizes worth Rs 10,00,000, along with paid internship opportunities at IIT Madras, IIITDM Kancheepuram, VIT-AP University and Shiv Nadar University, Chennai.

Billions of messages are protected every day by end-to-end encryption. But what happens when the cryptography is sound and the code around it is not?

Could you spot a weakened random-number generator or a quietly leaked key hidden in thousands of lines of code? Could you build a messaging system that holds up even when someone is actively trying to break it?

Protocol Zero: Boot | Hack | CTF is an opportunity to explore these challenges through a hands-on cybersecurity competition built around the Secure Communication Protocol and Signal Protocol.

Organised by IIT Madras in collaboration with IIITDM Kancheepuram, VIT-AP University, Shiv Nadar University, Chennai and DSCI, the program takes participants through multiple stages:

  • Mini-CTF: An online 24-hour cybersecurity challenge.
  • Bootcamp: Five days of expert-led training in applied cryptography and secure communication.
  • Hackathon: A six-week challenge focused on secure implementation, backdoor design and backdoor detection.
  • Final CTF: An onsite two-day Attack-Defence competition.

Top-performing teams will compete for cash prizes worth ₹10,00,000 and paid internship opportunities at IIT Madras and partner institutions.

If you are passionate about breaking systems, understanding vulnerabilities and engineering secure solutions, Protocol Zero is for you.


Eligibility Criteria

  • Open to currently enrolled undergraduate and postgraduate students from recognised institutions across India.
  • Each team must consist of a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 3 members.
  • Individual participation is not permitted.
  • Team members can belong to the same or different institutions.
  • Each participant can be part of only one team.
  • All participants must be at least 18 years old at the time of registration.
  • Participants must be willing to participate in all stages of the programme.

Competition Structure / Event Rounds

Round 1: Mini-CTF (Online - 24 Hours)

An online jeopardy-style Capture the Flag competition open to all eligible registered teams.

Challenges will cover:

  • Web Application Security
  • Cryptography and Cryptanalysis
  • Network Security and Traffic Analysis
  • Digital Forensics and Incident Investigation
  • Binary Exploitation and Reverse Engineering
  • Authentication and Access Control

The top 25 teams on the Mini-CTF scoreboard will qualify for the Bootcamp and Hackathon.

Round 2: Bootcamp (Online - 5 Days)

Shortlisted teams will participate in an intensive five-day Online Bootcamp featuring expert lectures and hands-on training in applied cryptography, secure communication protocols, and Secure Communication Protocol design and implementation. The Bootcamp will prepare teams for the Hackathon.

Round 3: Hackathon (Online - 6 Weeks)

Teams will work on a secure communication messaging environment across three technical tracks:

Track 1 - Secure Implementation
Build and harden a secure communication system ensuring confidentiality, integrity, authentication, forward secrecy and post-compromise security.

Track 2 - Backdoor Design (Red Team)
Demonstrate how subtle backdoors can be introduced into a secure implementation within a sandboxed test environment, with complete documentation.

Track 3 - Backdoor Detection (Blue Team)
Develop tools and techniques to identify backdoors and vulnerabilities using code auditing, static and dynamic analysis, fuzzing, differential testing and protocol conformance checks.

Every team must participate in all three tracks.

Submission Requirements:

  • Source Code
  • Technical Design Document
  • Demonstration Video

The top-performing teams will qualify for the Final CTF.

Round 4: Final CTF (Onsite - 2 Days)

The finalist teams will compete in an onsite CTF at Shiv Nadar University, Chennai. Teams will analyse Secure Communicationl-based implementations, including organiser-prepared and peer-submitted implementations, to identify planted backdoors and vulnerabilities while defending their own implementations. The event will conclude with final presentations before the jury, followed by the Grand Finale and Prize Distribution.

Round 5: Internship Opportunities

Top-performing participants will be offered internship opportunities at IIT Madras and partner institutions during Summer 2027.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Open to currently enrolled undergraduate and postgraduate students from recognised institutions across India.
  • Each team must consist of a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 3 members.
  • Individual participation is not permitted.
  • Team members can belong to the same or different institutions.
  • Each participant can be part of only one team.
  • All participants must be at least 18 years old at the time of registration.
  • Participants must be willing to participate in all stages of the programme.

Team Requirements

Minimum Team Size 2 members
Maximum Team Size 3 members
Participation Type Team-based
Individual Participation Not allowed
Cross-institutional Teams Allowed
Eligible Participants Undergraduate and postgraduate students
Geographic Eligibility Recognised institutions across India

Mandatory Registration Details

Every team member must provide the following information during registration. These details are required for all participants, not just the team leader:

  • Full Name
  • Valid Email Address
  • Contact Number
  • Resume / CV (PDF format)
  • GitHub Profile ID / URL

Important registration instructions:

  • Each team member must submit their individual details.
  • Ensure that all information provided is accurate and up to date.
  • Resume upload is mandatory for every participant.
  • Provide working link to the GitHub
  • Incomplete registrations may not be considered for shortlisting.

Selection Process

Mini-CTF Selection

The top 25 teams on the live Mini-CTF scoreboard will qualify for the Bootcamp and Hackathon. In case of a tie, the team with the earliest time of the last correct submission will be given preference.

Hackathon Selection

The top 25 teams based on the Hackathon evaluation will qualify for the onsite Final CTF. Final selection will be based on the evaluation criteria and scores assigned by the jury.

Code of Conduct

  • All participants must agree to and comply with the competition's Code of Conduct.
  • All offensive activities must be restricted strictly to the environment provided by the organisers.
  • Attacking competition infrastructure, other teams outside designated exercises, or any live/third-party systems is strictly prohibited.
  • Violations will result in immediate disqualification.

Originality and Submission Compliance

  • All submissions must be original work produced by the participating team.
  • Plagiarism and unauthorised use of third-party content are strictly prohibited.
  • All submissions must be completed within the specified deadlines.
  • Late submissions will not be accepted.

Judgement and Rule Modifications

  • The decisions of the judging panel shall be final and binding.
  • The organising institutions reserve the right to amend, modify or cancel any aspect of the event, including rules, dates, format and structure, without prior notice.
  • Detailed rules for each round will be published in due course.

Physical Presence for Final CTF

  • Teams qualifying for the Final CTF must be physically present at Shiv Nadar University, Chennai, on 12–13 March 2027.
  • Further logistical details will be communicated to shortlisted teams.

Intellectual Property Rights

  • Intellectual Property generated as part of the competition shall be owned by the organising institutions.
  • Participants will be duly recognised as inventors in any resulting patent applications, in accordance with IIT Madras IP policies.

By participating in Protocol Zero, all individuals and teams acknowledge and agree to these guidelines. Failure to comply may result in disqualification and forfeiture of associated benefits.
